chapter: Tiny Bradshaw, Teddy Hill and Europe
title: Dizzy Gillespie and the Teddy Hill band members on the boat to Europe
summary: Procope remembers Dizzy as a clown in a hat and overcoat on deck, and lists the band including Dicky Wells, Bill Dillard and Shad Collins, which recorded.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Was Dizzy Gillespie with Teddy Hill then?
Yes. Dizzy Gillespie. Dicky Wells.
And I guess Dizzy was sounding like Roy Eldridge.
He sounded like everybody. Rex Stewart and -- yeah. Yeah. I remember going over on the boat. On the boat Dizzy -- well, this one time in particular I remember, he
got up, you know, we were all lounging around the deck, so here comes Dizzy all dressed up with his overcoat on and his hat, so we all said to him, "Hey, Diz, you going somewhere?"
(Laughter)
Yeah, Dizzy was a real fun guy.
Was he just as much of a clown then?
Yeah. Yeah.
(Inaudible)
Yeah. Someone asked me where did he get the name Dizzy. I said, "Well, I really don't know. I suppose somebody, you know, when he was a kid --"
Because he was dizzy.
Maybe something like that, yeah.
(Inaudible)

Yeah, we had Dizzy and Bob Carroll. Bob Carroll was a tenor player. He played tenor and Howard Johnson was the other alto player, and we had Shad Collins, (Richard) a trumpet player. Bill Dillard and Dizzy. Fullbright was the bass player. John Smith was the guitar player.
This was the band that recorded.
Yeah, at that time we recorded, yeah.
So that was your first time to Europe.
Yeah. Yeah.
That must have been an experience.
